blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
British manners, at their most refined, are a kind of grammar — an unwritten set of rules about how to interact that signal belonging and recognition. They are learned slowly, often unconsciously, and rarely explained directly. But they are very real, and they shape how senior British colleagues decide, over time, who is 'one of us' and who is not.

Some of these rules are small and almost invisible: saying 'thank you' twice in a doorway rather than once, apologising for bumping into someone who bumped into you, offering to make the next round of tea. Others are larger: how to handle a colleague's personal difficulty, how to congratulate a rival without sounding false, how to enter and leave a room when the most senior person is still speaking.

Never are these rules written in a handbook. Rarely are they taught in a training session. They are picked up by watching, by being gently corrected, and by eventually becoming fluent in a style of courtesy that looks effortless but is, in fact, a lifetime of small, deliberate choices.

items.q: According to the text, what do refined British manners most resemble?
items.why: "British manners, at their most refined, are a kind of grammar" — regras não escritas que se dominam com o tempo.

items.q: How are these rules usually acquired?
options: By asking senior colleagues to explain them directly
Through a written manual issued on the first day
By watching, being gently corrected, and gradually becoming fluent
items.why: "They are picked up by watching, by being gently corrected…"

items.q: The phrase "who is 'one of us' and who is not" suggests that manners function as…
options: a marker of who belongs to the group
items.why: Inferência: as maneiras sinalizam pertencimento (belonging) — quem é aceito no grupo e quem não é.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Courtesy that looks effortless often conceals years of practice.
Good manners can be mastered by reading the company handbook.
Small gestures can carry real social weight.
The most important rules of etiquette are rarely spelled out.
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma que essas regras NÃO estão em manual algum — são apreendidas na convivência.

items.q: What does the observation that courtesy "looks effortless but is, in fact, a lifetime of small, deliberate choices" imply?
options: Manners are ultimately unimportant at senior level
The apparent naturalness is the product of sustained, conscious effort
The ease is genuine and requires no thought
Only people born into it can ever manage it
items.why: Inferência: a naturalidade aparente esconde escolhas deliberadas acumuladas ao longo da vida.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte preparando um executivo estrangeiro para a primeira semana. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right — a few things before Monday, and none of them are in any induction pack, which is rather the point.

This is an old institution, and here manners are watched with quiet attention. Nobody will ever correct you out loud. Seldom will anyone tell you what you did wrong; they simply notice, and they remember. So watch the room before you speak. If the most senior person is still talking, you do not get up, you do not check your phone, and you certainly do not leave.

Two small habits will carry you a long way. Thank people twice, not once — in the doorway, over the tea, whenever a kindness is done. And when something goes wrong, apologise first, even if it was plainly not your fault. It sounds absurd, I know, but here it reads as grace, not weakness.

One last thing. When you congratulate a rival — and you will have to — say it plainly and move on. Overdo it and it sounds false. Understate it and it sounds cold. The right word, at the right moment, said once and meant. Get that rhythm, and you will be fine.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Charlotte point out that none of her advice is "in any induction pack"?
options: The company forgot to write an induction pack
The most important rules here are unwritten, which is precisely her point
The pack is being revised this week
She wants him to read the pack more carefully
items.why: "none of them are in any induction pack, which is rather the point" — as regras que importam são não escritas.

items.q: What does Charlotte say will happen if you make a mistake in manners?
options: You will be corrected loudly and immediately
A senior colleague will explain the rule privately
Nobody will tell you, but they will notice and remember
items.why: "Seldom will anyone tell you what you did wrong; they simply notice, and they remember."

items.q: Why does Charlotte advise apologising first, even when it was not your fault?
options: Because it shifts the blame elsewhere
Because in this setting it reads as grace, not weakness
items.why: "here it reads as grace, not weakness" — pedir desculpas sinaliza cortesia, não fraqueza.

items.q: What does Charlotte imply about congratulating a rival?
options: It should be as effusive as possible
It is best done in writing only
The tone must be calibrated — neither overdone nor cold
items.why: Inferência: "Overdo it and it sounds false. Understate it and it sounds cold" — o acerto está no equilíbrio.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's overall message?
options: Manners here are relaxed and rarely noticed
The executive should simply be himself and ignore convention
Following the written handbook is enough to fit in
Senior courtesy is a matter of precise, deliberate restraint
items.why: Inferência: seu conselho gira em torno de gestos precisos e contidos — a cortesia como precisão.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "His delivery was effortless, though everyone knew he had rehearsed for weeks." Effortless here means…
items.why: Effortless = que parece não exigir esforço — mesmo quando há muito trabalho por trás.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every small courtesy was a ___ choice, never an accident."
items.why: Deliberate = deliberado, intencional — o oposto de acidental.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A quiet nod from the chairman was enough to signal ___ — the newcomer had been accepted."
items.why: Belonging = pertencimento, o sentido de fazer parte do grupo.

items.q: "These norms form an unwritten grammar of the office." Unwritten means the rules are…
options: not set down in writing yet very real
items.why: Unwritten = não escrito; existem e valem, mas não estão registradas em lugar nenhum.

items.q: "Her thanks carried a warmth that read as genuine recognition." Recognition here means…
options: acknowledgement of someone's worth or contribution
items.why: Recognition = reconhecimento: o ato de valorizar e acolher alguém.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que circulam em ambientes executivos britânicos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Never have I seen a room fall silent so quickly." This fronted, inverted structure is used to…
options: add emphasis and a formal register
items.why: Fronting negativo (never/rarely/seldom) inverte a frase e eleva o registro, dando ênfase — a gramática da lição.

items.q: "The chairman quietly picked up on the newcomer's slip." To pick up on something means to…
options: notice or become aware of it
items.why: Pick up on = perceber, captar algo sutil — sem necessariamente comentar.

items.q: "You'll need to read the room before you speak." To read the room means to…
options: sense the mood and adjust accordingly
items.why: Read the room = sentir o clima do ambiente e se ajustar a ele.

items.q: "Don't lay it on too thick when you congratulate a rival." This warns you not to…
items.why: Lay it on too thick = exagerar nos elogios, a ponto de soar falso.

items.q: "Seldom does a newcomer find their feet so quickly." To find your feet means to…
options: become comfortable and confident in a new situation
items.why: Find your feet = se adaptar, ganhar segurança num ambiente novo.
